name: Merchant Pool device fingerprint script (Microsoft DFP)

story.what_it_is: A script from a LinkedIn server runs a device fingerprint check tied to your browser ID.
story.for_you: You never see it. A script collects clues about your device, such as screen and software traits, to build a fingerprint. Public analysis suggests it comes from Microsoft's fraud tools.
story.for_makers: A device fingerprint lets a platform tell if the same device creates many fake accounts or ads. It works even when cookies are cleared. The same trick can also track a person across visits, which is why privacy groups push back.

use_cases.example: A fraudster opens twenty fake ad accounts from one laptop. The fingerprint links them as one device.
A stolen card is used to buy ads, and the fingerprint helps spot the device behind many cards.
A banned account owner comes back with a new email, and the device fingerprint links the new account to the old one.
A person makes many accounts to cheat on a game leaderboard, and a fingerprint can reveal one device behind them.
Ad review teams use the fingerprint to remove clicks from the same device that clicks the same ad hundreds of times.
An analytics team counts unique devices rather than cookies, which stays steady after people clear cookies.

risks: Cannot be easily reset by you
